items.quote: it is the dutie of the parents, euen in the infancie, to begin to shape and frame the foule vnto vertue

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.

items.text: Reverence him and stand in a reverend awe of him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: that she reuerence her husband

items.text: Submit yourself to him and be obedient to him, even if he is not a believer.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she submit herselfe, and be obedient vnto him

items.text: Do not wear gorgeous apparel beyond your degree and place; let your attire be comely and sober according to your calling.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: that she do not weare gorgeous apparell, beyond her degree and place, but that her attire be comely and sober, according to her calling.

items.text: Be serviceable and obedient to him, careful to please him and loath to offend him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: to reuerence them, and to endeuour with true obedience and loue to serue them; to be loth in any wise to offend them

items.text: If you have angered or displeased him, never rest until you have pacified him and regained his favor.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she ought neuer to rest vntill she haue pacified him, and gotten his fauour againe.

items.text: If he blames you without cause, bear it patiently, give no unkind word, and look on him with a loving and cheerful countenance, taking the fault upon yourself rather than seeming displeased.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she must beare it patiently, and giue him no vncomely or vnkind word for it; but euermore looke vpon him with a louing and cheerefull countenance

items.text: Always be merry and cheerful in his company, but not with too much lightness; beware of swelling, pouting, lowering, or frowning.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Let her be alwaies merry and cheerfull in his company, but yet not with too much lightnesse. She must beware in any wise of swelling, powting, lowring, or frowning

items.text: Be quick and cleanly about his meat and drink, preparing it according to his diet in due season; let nothing be spilt or go to waste through your negligence.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she must be quicke and cleanly about her husbands meare and drinke, preparing him the same according to his diet in due season.

items.text: Show yourself in word and deed wise, humble, courteous, gentle, and loving toward him and toward those he loves.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Let her shew her selfe in word and deed wise, humble, curteous, gentle, and louing towards her husband, and also towards such as he doth loue

items.text: Love no man so well as your husband; love none other at all but him, unless it be for his sake and the Lord's.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Let her shew her selfe not onely to loue no man so well as her husband, but also to loue none other at all but him

items.text: Love him none otherwise than yourself, for you are one body with him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she is one bodie with her husband; so that she ought to loue him none otherwise then her selfe

items.text: Reckon your husband as father, mother, brother, and sister to you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: the wife should reckon, to haue her husband for both father, mother, brother, and sister

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.

items.text: Be an example to her in temperance, quietness, chastity, diligence, and religion, and never command what you will not do yourself.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: if he command any thing to be done, he must looke that he deny not to do the same himselfe

items.text: Never strike her or come near blows; think your anger too much, for you may not hate your own flesh.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: God saith, nay: thou mayest not hate thy wife: For no man hateth his owne flesh; shewing that he should not come neare blowes

items.text: Treat her as a companion and friend, not as a servant; your fellowship should be greater than that between father and son.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: such society and fellowship, yea and greater, then is betweene the father and the sonne; and not such as is betweene the maister and the seruant.

items.text: Rule not by compulsion or force; seek agreement in will and mind, for there can be no quiet marriage without it.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: there cannot be any quiet marriage or vnitie, where he and his wife do not agree in will and minde

items.text: Dwell with her in godly peace; avoid strife, for a divided house cannot stand and strife leaves only dust and ashes.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: an house cannot stand if it be diuided: for strife is like a fire, which leaues nothing but dust, smoke, and ashes behind it.

items.text: Do not threaten or handle her roughly; do not use her as a servant, for cruelty turns her love into hatred.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: through euill and rough handling, and in threatning of their wiues, haue and vse them not as wiues, but as their seruants

items.text: In the first year of marriage, stay home to learn her character and settle your love, rather than going to war.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: God would not haue the husband go to warre with his enemies, to the end that he and his wife might learne to know one anothers conditions and qualities

items.text: Honor her as your crown; wounding her wounds your own honor.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: Salomon calleth the wife, The crowne of her husband. Therefore he which woundeth her, woundeth his owne honour

items.text: Remember that marriage is friendship, not tyranny; do not compel her body or will.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1
items.quote: marriage is the supreme and most excellent part of all amitie and friendship: and that it farre differeth from tyranny

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: A GODLY FORME OF HOVSHOLD GOVERNMENT: CAREFVLLY TO be practised of all Christian Housholders.

items.text: Provide honestly for your household; avoid borrowing, usury, and suretiship.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: To auoide borrowing, a good husband must cut off all vnnecessarie expences, that he may haue all necessaries in his house.

items.text: Keep none idle; assign each a charge that occupies him, inspect their work, and trust them only as you see them unless they fear God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: keepe none in his house idle... let euery one haue his charge... trust them not further then you see them.

items.text: Help your husband in providing for the household as God made you his helper.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: she must help him in the prouision for her family, so much as lieth in her power, and is meete for to do.

items.text: Be subject to him; let him rule the household, especially outward affairs, and do not oppose him even if he errs.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: if she be not subiect to her husband, to let him rule all the hous-hold, especially outward affaires... God will not blesse where his ordinance is not obeyed.

items.text: Be content with the apparel and outward estate his means allow; do not importune for more.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: be content with such apparell and outward port as her husbands estate can allow her. They faile in this, who by importunitie and disquietnesse, wring from their husbands more.

items.text: Be faithful; do not secretly take from him to dress up yourself or your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: It is a part of unthankfulnesse, secretly to purloyne and powle from him, for to prancke vp her children, or her selfe, her house, and chambers in brauerie.

items.text: Love him and be peaceable toward him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: Loue and peaceablenesse in the wife towards her husband, is auaileable for the weale of the family.

items.text: Settle disagreements privately and quickly; use no hard words or reopening of old matters.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: Let there be therefore reasonings secretly betweene themselues... and let them be soone ended... Let there be no hard words of either side, not opening of old matters.

items.text: Keep your disputes private, not before children, lest they carry tales and lose regard for you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: Let it be done priuately betweene themselues, and not before children, or seruants: for they will not sticke to carrie tales.

items.text: Keep your disputes private, not before servants, lest they carry tales and lose regard for you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: Let it be done priuately betweene themselues, and not before children, or seruants: for they will not sticke to carrie tales.

items.text: Hear your wife's advice and follow it when it is good.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
items.quote: a wise husband will not disdaine to heare her aduice, and follow it also, if it be good.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.

items.text: Do not put away your wife for any cause, except for whoredom, duly proved before a lawful judge.
items.citation: Godly Forme, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: no man may put away his wife for any cause, except for whoredome

items.text: Commend your marriage to God by humble and fervent prayer, that he would bless you in it.
items.citation: Godly Forme, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: commend their state and marriage to God, by humble and feruent prayer

items.text: Live together with all care and heedfulness, that you have no need of such a medicine as divorce.
items.citation: Godly Forme, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: with all care and heedfulnesse so to liue in marriage, that they haue no need of such a medicine

items.text: Submit to your husband as to the Lord, obeying him in good and right.
items.citation: Godly Forme, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Wiues submit your selues vnto your husbands as to the Lord

items.text: Take your husband as your head and governor, calling him Lord as Sarah did.
items.citation: Godly Forme, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: the daughters of Sarah are bound to call their husbands Lord, as Sarah called her husband

items.text: Bear rule in your own house, as head.
items.citation: Godly Forme, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: euery man should beare rule in his owne house

items.text: Nurse your own children yourself, and do not put them out to nursing.
items.citation: Godly Forme, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: naturall mothers to nourish their children with their owne milke

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.

items.text: Enter the marriage contract with a willing and unfeigned consent from the heart.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: it must not come from the lips alone, but from the wel-liking and consent of the heart

items.text: Make your marriage promise to him as he makes his to you, willingly and mutually.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: it must be a mutuall promise, that is, either party must make it to other

items.text: Before giving your child in marriage, ask her consent.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: We will call the maide, and aske her consent

items.text: Persuade your child to consent to marriage by good means, not by force or trickery.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: It becometh the parents to perswade their children by all good meanes to yeeld their consent, rather then to draw them by wicked sleights and cunning

items.text: If you compelled your child into a marriage promise, break that promise and set them free.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: ought to be frustrated & broken, by the parents themselues

items.text: Lead and guide her in all things, for you are her head and she is your glory.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: he is her head, and she his glory: and ought to leade and guide her in all things

items.text: Leave your father and mother and be joined to your wife.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: Therefore a man shall leaue his father and mother, and shall be ioyned to his wife, and they two shall be one flesh

items.text: Give up authority over your own body to your wife, and take authority over hers.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: the man hath not power ouer his owne body, nor the woman ouer hers

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Provide that your children learn at least to write and read.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: prouide that their children may learne, at the least to write and rcade

items.text: Have your children read some chapters of the Holy Scriptures daily.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: vse them daily to reade some Chapters of the holy Scriptures

items.text: Instruct your children in the knowledge and fear of God and in the faith of Jesus Christ.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: instruct their children in the knowledge and feare ofGod, and in the faith of Iesus Christ

items.text: Teach your children what they will need to use in their age.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: teach them those things which they are to vse in their age

items.text: Bring up your children in some course, trade, or other estate to earn a living.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: bring vp their children in some course, trade, or other estate, wherein to get their liuings

items.text: If you are unable to instruct them yourself, arrange for godly others to do so, else you are inexcusable.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: if they be neither able of thēselues, nor do prouide to haue them taught by others, they shall be inexcusable

items.text: Begin in tender youth to frame and bend your children to virtue.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: begin to frame and bend their children in their tender youth to vertue

items.text: Do not speak foolish tales, bawdy rhymes, or ungodly speeches before your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: be carefull that they do not speake or tell any foolish tales, baudie rimes, or vngodly speeches before their children

items.text: Restrain your children from conversing with vicious and wicked companions.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: restraine their children from haunting and conuersing with such as be vicious, peruerse, and wicked

items.text: When placing your children with a trade master or teacher, ensure he is religious, virtuous, and fears God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: ought carefully to see and enquire whether such as they thinke to place them withall, be religious and vertuous, and endued with the feare of God

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.

items.text: Be subject to your husband as the church is to Christ.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: be subiect to her husband, Ephes. 5. 22. Colloss. 3. 18. 1. Pet. 3. 1.

items.text: Be chaste, shamefast, modest, silent, godly, and discreet.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: To be chast and shamefast, modest and silent, godly and discreet.

items.text: Keep yourself at home to oversee the good government of your family, and do not go out without just cause.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: keepe her selfe at home for the good gouernment of her family, and not to stray abroad without iust cause.

items.text: Nurse your own child yourself rather than handing him to a stranger, unless just cause prevents it.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: refuse this so necessary a duty of a mother due to her children.

items.text: Use your breasts as a help to your husband in suckling the child you share.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: to be a helpe to her husband in suckling the child common to them both.

items.text: Bear with your husband patiently.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: patience to suffer her husband.

items.text: Love your children and bring them up.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: loue to breed and bring vp her children.

items.text: Govern your house with wisdom.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: wisedome to gouerne her house.

items.text: Be diligent to save and put aside the goods in your charge.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: diligence, to lay vp, and to saue such goods as are within her charge.

items.text: Carry yourself with gravity when you go out in public.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: haue grauitie when she walketh abroad.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Bring them up in learning or in some trade or handicraft, so that they may earn a living and live well.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: parents do bring vp their children, either in learning, or in some occupation and handycraft, whereby they may get their liuing another day, and so liue the better.

items.text: Keep them from idleness as from a plague or contagious disease.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: let all Christian parents therefore labour and endeuour to auoyd it, both in themselues and their children, as a plague, or contagious disease.

items.text: Teach them to know God rightly and how he will be served.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: especially when they are taught to know God aright, and how he will be serued.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.

items.text: Aid and help each other as companions joined by God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: the dutie common both to the husband and wife, importeth, that the one should aide and helpe the other.

items.text: Live together in chastity and purity, keeping the marriage bed undefiled.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: liue together in all chastitie and purenesse, and that they take great heed and beware of breaking the bond.

items.text: Avoid all appearances, allurements, and occasions of evil that might provoke lust or jealousy.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: forbeare from euery thing that may seeme to tend thereunto, or to continue any beginning, apparence, allurement, or occasion of euill.

items.text: Labor in your calling and bring in provision for your family.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: the husband is to get it, and to bring it in

items.text: Order and dispose household goods, and also help your husband in his labor as you are able, without controlling him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: the wife to order and dispose it... she also, according to her ability and power, must helpe her husband to get it

items.text: Guide her in household management with discretion, not meddling contemptuously with her small affairs.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: in his discretion, direct her in the dispensation thereof, and not meddle with her small houshold affaires.

items.text: Do not be idle or unthrifty, and avoid alehouses, lest you become cruel to your wife and children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: an idle and vnthrifty husband... if idlenesse draw him to loue and haunt ale-houses and tauernes, is cruell to his wife and children

items.text: Do not be prodigal or slothful, for you bring reproach and poverty to your husband and household.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: a prodigall and slothfull wife... confounds her husband, and bringeth reproach and pouertie to her whole family.

items.text: If your wife is wasteful, be patient, admonish her discreetly, and pray to God for her.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: The remedy for the husband that hath such a wife, is patience, with discret admonition and prayer to God

items.text: If your husband is idle, tolerate him, gently exhort him, and cheerfully welcome him home to keep him from taverns.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: tolleration, gentle exhortation, and cheerefull and louing entertainment of her husband, whereby to enduce him willingly to keepe home.

items.text: Labor for each other's salvation and growth in godliness: win an unbelieving spouse, and confirm and strengthen a believing spouse.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: if one of them... be an vnbeleeuer, the other must labour to draw his partie to the knowledge of the truth

items.text: Be instructed yourself, and ready to instruct your wife at home, gathering good instruction to impart to her.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: the husband ought to be so instructed, as that he may be ready to instruct his wife at home

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Train them up in the study of virtue and of a godly life.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: traine them vp in the study of vertue, and of a godly life.

items.text: Warn your child of spiritual dangers and teach him to resist the devil and call upon God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Oh my sonne, vnderstand what God hath done for thy sake. Take heed to thy selfe. The world is all ouer-strewed with snares.

items.text: Do not allow your child to have his own will, but restrain and govern him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: not to suffer their children and youth to haue their owne will

items.text: Provide your child wholesome and sufficient food, not pampering him with excess or delicacies.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: moderation in diet; not to pamper children with too much meate, or that which is delicate, but to giue them that which is wholesome and sufficient

items.text: Do not clothe your child in costly or fashionable apparel, but in modest attire.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: not to cloath them with costly apparell, or to attire them with new fashions

items.text: Reprove and correct your child, and continue to exercise fatherly authority as long as you have a child.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: reprehension, or chiding... so long as thou hast a child, so long thou art a parent: and so long as thou art a father, so long thou must carry a fatherly authoritie and power ouer him.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.

items.text: Love her as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife
items.quote: shew thy selfe vnto her, as Christ shewed himselfe vnto his Church

items.text: Keep the marriage bed undefiled; let your embraces be chaste.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife
items.quote: Matrimonie is a thing sanctified of God, the which willeth the matrimoniall imbracements to be chast, the bed to be vndefiled

items.text: Regard her as your companion and helper, not as a servant, and value her faithful service.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife
items.quote: thy wife will be led onely by loue, and therefore she doth euery thing better then all other

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Children towards their Parents.

items.text: Obey, serve, fear, love, honour, and reverence your parents in word, deed, heart, and mind.
items.citation: A Godly Forme, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: obey their parents, and do serue them, and also do feare, loue, honour, and reuerence them; not onely in word and deed, but in their hearts and minds also.

items.text: Follow their good precepts and examples of life.
items.citation: A Godly Forme, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: follow their good precepts and examples of life.

items.text: Patiently take correction at their hands.
items.citation: A Godly Forme, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: patiently take correction at their hands.

items.text: Make continual and hearty prayers to God for them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: make continuall and hearty prayers to God for them.

items.text: Relieve, maintain, and nourish them if they fall into poverty or decay.
items.citation: A Godly Forme, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: do relieue, maintaine, and nourish their parents, in case they shall fall into pouertie or decay.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Make good and honest provision, according to your degree, for the relief and maintenance of your children and family.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: make good and honest prouision... for the reliefe and maintenance of their children and familie

items.text: Be careful that your sons and daughters do not marry the ungodly or those void of true religion.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: be very wary and carefull, that their sonnes and daughters do not match in marriage with such as are vngodly

items.text: Sow the seed of virtue in your children in their youth, teaching them to remember their Creator.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Remember now thy Creator, in the dayes of thy youth

items.text: Give your children good education; do not neglect it.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: prophanely neglected all good education

items.text: Do not allow your children to do evil to others; correct them as you would correct wrongs done to yourself.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: suffered their children iniuriously to do euill to others, which they could not suffer to do to themselues

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.

items.text: Please your husband's nature, inclinations, and manners, as long as they import no wickedness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: there is a certaine discretion and desire required of women, to please the nature, inclinations, and manners of their husbands, so long as the same import no wickednesse.

items.text: Obey your husband's manners as men obey the laws of their cities, and be attentive to his smallest sign of displeasure.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: as men should obey the lawes of their Cities, so women the manners of their husbands.

items.text: Love your house; do not gad from house to house to prate, but go abroad only for holy meetings, visiting the needy, household affairs, or when your husband requires you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: the woman that gaddeth from house to house to prate, confoundeth her selfe, her husband and family

items.text: Be silent, obedient, peaceable, patient, studious to appease your husband's anger, and diligent in your business.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: to be silent, obedient, peaceable, patient, studious to appease his choler if he be angry, painefull, and diligent in looking to her businesse

items.text: Govern your wife wisely, discreetly, and well, and give her a good example in word and deed.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: the want and neglect of the wise, discreet, and good gouernment that should be in the husbands: besides the want of good example that they should giue vnto their wiues

items.text: Be of one heart, will, and mind; do not upbraid each other's wants or pride yourselves in gifts, but supply each other's wants.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: They must be of one heart, will, and mind, and neither to vpbraide or cast the other in the teeth with their wants and imperfections

items.text: Faithfully serve each other, keep no secrets, do not publish each other's frailties, share all goods in common, and be loving, kind, courteous, and gentle.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: the one faithfully serueth the other: when in things concerning marriage, the one hideth no secrets nor priuities from the other

items.text: Be obsequious, diligent, and serviceable to each other in all honest things, observing what pleases or displeases the other.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Let the one learne euer to be obsequious, diligent, and seruiceable to the other in all honest things.

items.text: If one is angry, let the other open the grief in due time and with discretion; do not speak when out of patience.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: if one of them be angry, and offended with the other, then let the party grieued open and make knowne vnto the other their griefe in due time, and with discretion.

items.text: Do not forsake each other's company because of offenses, like one who forsakes honey because stung by bees.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: the one be not so offended... that they should thereupon forsake the company one of another: for that were like to one that being stung with the Bees, would therefore forsake the bony.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.

items.text: Rejoice with him in his joys and weep with him in his griefs.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: With whom should the wife reioyce, rather then with her louing husband? Or with whome, should she weepe and mourne, rather then with her owne flesh?

items.text: Never leave him until death.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: I will neuer leaue him till death.

items.text: Bear his burdens as he bears yours.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Who shall beare one anothers burthen, if the wife do not beare the husbands burden?

items.text: Comfort him in sickness and seek his health.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Wicked lezabel comforted her husband in his sicknesse: and Ieroboams wife sought for his health

items.text: Be a yoke-fellow, sharing his labors and troubles.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she was content not onely to be his play fellow, but his yoke-fellow too.

items.text: Help him in his labors, troubles, and sickness, with your strength and counsel.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she is called an helper, to helpe him in his labours, to helpe him in his troubles, to helpe him in his sicknesse

items.text: Be a comfort to him, causing him to rejoice.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: wiues must be the reioycing of their husbands, euen like Dauids harpe to comfort Saul.

items.text: Obey him and love him even if he is foolish or churlish, and let your words, deeds, and countenance be such as he loves.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: being bound she must obey: as Abigail loued her husband, though he were a foole, churlish, and euill conditioned.

items.text: Do not take rule over him, but keep your subordinate standing.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: It beseemeth not the mistresse to be maister, no more then it becommeth the maister to be mistresse

items.text: Keep at home, be chaste, and do not wander about.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: Paul biddeth Titus to exhort women that they be chast, and keeping at home

items.text: Ask his leave before going abroad, even on good errands.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband
items.quote: she did aske her husband leaue to go vnto the Prophet... yet she thought it not meete to go farre abroad without her husbands leaue

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Declare your instruction in holy life and virtuous conversation, ordering yourselves so that your children may see it and be restrained from dishonest speech and wicked deeds.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: declare the same in holy life and vertuous conuersation: let them so order and gouerne themselues, that their children seeing the same, as it were in a glasse, may be restrained from dishonest speech

items.text: Feed, nourish, and bring up your children.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: They be charged by the fift Commandement, to feede, to nourish, and to bring vp their children

items.text: Teach them the principles and seeds of Christian religion, and see that they learn the catechism.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: to teach them the principles and seede of Christian religion, to see they learne the Catechisme

items.text: Teach them to praise God before and after meals.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: to teach them to praise God before and after meales

items.text: Teach them little by little and by often repetitions to understand why the sacraments were instituted.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: to teach them by little and little, and by often repetitions, to vnderstand wherefore the Sacraments were instituted

items.text: Teach them good manners: how to behave decently in walking, speaking, and bodily gesture, reverently in church, and civilly toward all men.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: to teach them manners how to behaue themselues decently in their going, in their speaking, and gesture of their bodies: how to order themselues reuerently in the Church, how abroad in all places, and towards all men in all honest companies

items.text: Begin to form a conscience in them, for it were better for children to be unborn than untaught.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: begin some conscience in them. For it were better for children to be vnborne then vntaught

items.text: Correct them when they do amiss, and keep them in shamefastness, hatred of vice, and love of all virtue.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: correct them when they do amisse, & keepe them in shamefastnesse, hatred of vice, & loue of all vertue

items.text: Hold your children in awe, and they will have you in reverence.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: Hold thy children in awe, and they shall haue thee in reuerence

items.text: Bestow diligent labor that your children be forthwith instructed in virtue and godliness while their age is tender and tractable.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: prouide, and bestow diligent labour, that their children be foorthwith instructed in vertue and godlinesse, whilest their wits are yet voide from cares and vices, and whilest their age is tender and tractable

items.text: See that your children are carefully brought up in the fear of God, for they are God's children.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: they shall do great iniurie to God himselfe whose children they are, if they shall not see them carefully brought vp in his feare

items.text: Do not bequeath or consecrate your children to monasteries, friaries, or nunneries, where they would remain in bondage of ignorance and idolatry.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: bequeath them, & in a manner, consecrate & sacrifice them to the seruice of men, by thrusting thē into Abbeyes, Munkeries, Fryeries, Nunneries, and Seminaries

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.

items.text: Do not displease your husband by overmuch rehearsing your first husband; live by the living, not the dead.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: do not displease their wiues or their husbands which they now haue, by ouermuch rehearsing of their first wife or first husband

items.text: Love, tender, and cherish your stepchildren as your own, as a true father or mother would.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: they ought to loue them, to tender them, and to cherish them, as their owne father or mother did

items.text: Dress soberly and modestly, avoiding gorgeous apparel and braided hair trimmed with gold; be adorned with a meek and quiet spirit.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: do not weare gorgeous and sumptuous apparell, or broidered haire trimmed with gold

items.text: Do not suffer or tolerate your wife's pride and excess in apparel; rule your household so that she dresses soberly.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: their husbands for suffering this great wickednesse and dissolutenesse in their wiues

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Teach your child the knowledge of God and bring him up in virtue and the fear of God.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: instruct him in the way of godlinesse, and so leaue him a vertuous consceince

items.text: Instruct your child not only in godliness but also in all other human duties, that he may learn the trade of his way.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: not onely to instruct him vnto godlinesse, but also vnto all other humane duties

items.text: Observe carefully to what vices your child is inclined, and admonish him and draw him from his sin.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: carefully obserue, vnto what vices their children are most inclined, and so by good meanes admonish and draw them from their sinne

items.text: Be more careful to provide spiritual things for your child's soul than temporal things for his body.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: so much more carefull ought they to be to prouide spiritual things for their soules

items.text: Guard your child's soul from vices and false doctrine when he comes to years of discretion.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: take care, that their soules be not poysoned with vices, and false and erronious doctrine

items.text: Perform the duty of parents to all children committed to your charge, as if they were your own.
items.citation: Godly Forme, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: bound by the voyce of the Almighty, to performe and to do the dutie of parents, to all such as are committed to their charge

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Bring them up in a virtuous and godly education, that they may become good parents after you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: endeauour to go forward in this vertuous education of your children

items.text: Do not disinherit him without grave cause; acknowledge his right of the firstborn and give him a double portion.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: the eldest had double so much as the others, of the fathers goods, and alone to the eldest pertained the blessing of the father

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.

items.text: Submit yourself to your husband as to the Lord, for he is your head.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: wiues submit themselues, and be obedient vnto their owne husbands as to the Lord

items.text: Obey your husband in all things not contrary to God's word.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: The obedience that the wife oweth to her husband

items.text: Set aside your own will and discretion, and follow your husband's judgment as your head.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: she shall haue no other discretion or will, but what may depend vpon her head

items.text: Submit even your vows to your husband, for he has authority to disallow them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: if the woman had vowed any thing vnto God, it should not withstanding rest in her husband to disauow it

items.text: Use your knowledge and discretion for your husband's good, but always in submission to him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: for the good of her husband: but alwayes it must be with condition to submit herselfe unto him

items.text: Let your wisdom and words be expressed as through your husband, not independently.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: all that she knoweth, and can do, is, as if it were said and done by her husband

items.text: Do not provoke your husband by disobedience in matters that may be done without offense to God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: women may not prouoke their husbands by disobedience, in matters that may be performed without offence to God

items.text: Do not presume over your husband because of your kindred or wealth.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: neither presume ouer them, either in kindred or wealth

items.text: Do not obstinately refuse in a matter that may trouble household peace.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: obstinately to refuse in a matter that may trouble household peace and quiet

items.text: If obedience is difficult, you may gently present your case, but obey if he persists, as long as it is not wickedness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: she may for her excuse gently propound: yet vpon condition to obey, in case the husband should persist in his intent, so long as the discommoditie importeth no wickednesse

items.text: Choose to keep peace by obedience rather than break it by resistance.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: it is better to continue peace by obedience, then to breake it by resistance

items.text: Obey only what is comely in the Lord, refusing commands contrary to your honor, credit, or salvation.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What the dutie of a wife is toward her husband.
items.quote: must not this obedience so farre extend, as that the husband should command any thing contrary to her honour, credit, and saluation, but as it is comely in the Lord

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Before committing your child to a master, inquire into his honesty and Christian conversation, lest the child be corrupted.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: if parents shall commit their child to the ordering and instruction of a maister, before they make enquirie of his honestie and Christian conuersation

items.text: Choose a master for your child for his virtue, not for friendship, worldly advancement, or low cost.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: others commit their children either to him that will take them at the easiest rate, or by whom they may grow into greatest aduancement

items.text: Restrain your child from vice and accustom him to virtue.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: Let them also be carefull to restraine their children from vice, and to inure and accustome them to vertue

items.text: Instruct your child, or cause him to be instructed, in the way he should go.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: the fathers that instruct, or cause their children to be instructed, do far excell such as onely do beget them

items.text: Do not merely rely on the master's diligence, but see how your child profits in learning and virtue.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: parents ought not so much to relie and rest vpon the diligence of their childrens maisters, as neuer to care to vnderstand how they profit and go forward in learning and vertue

items.text: Perform your duty to your child with moderation, gravity, and authority.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: Parents must performe their dutie to their children moderately, with great grauity and authority.

items.text: Teach your child to know God and to know himself.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: teach their children to know God, and to know themselues

items.text: Reprove your child when he does amiss.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: reproue them when they do amisse

items.text: Practice godliness and honesty yourself, that your child may learn by your example.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: they must be diligent and carefull to practise godlinesse & honesty themselues

items.text: Do not use lewd speeches or shameless behavior in the presence of your child, lest your example license him to do the same.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: shall vse any leude speeches, or shamelesse behauiour: in briefe, any worldly or carnall actions in the presence of their children

items.text: Do not commit the faults you forbid and correct in your child, lest your authority be diminished.
items.citation: Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: how can they forbid that in their children, which they themselues do commit? How can they correct them for the faults which they themselues vse?

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Provide a fit and skillful schoolmaster to instruct them in virtue, wisdom and good learning.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: prouide a meete and fit Schoole-maister to further the same.

items.text: Do not spare cost for a good schoolmaster, but maintain him as carefully as you would a good horse-keeper.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: euen so much more ought Christian parents to be desirous to haue, and maintaine a good Schoolemaister, that might bring vp their children in vertue, wisedome and good learning.

items.text: See that there is no fault in the teacher to whom you commit their upbringing in learning and good manners.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: looke that there be no fault in the teacher, to whom they commit the care to bring them vp in learning and good manners.

items.text: Do not hinder them from continuing their studies to good perfection because of lack of worldly advantage or trouble.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: yet will they not suffer them to continue thereat vntill they come to any good perfection

items.text: Teach them Moses and the Prophets, admonish them, and show them the danger of God's heavy displeasure.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: you will not teach them Moses & the Prophets: and you will not shew them the danger of Gods heauie displeasure

items.text: Bring them up well and virtuously, for such children as you bring up, such parents will they be after you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: if you will bring them vp well and vertuously, they shall be the better for it all their liues after

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Do not consent to your child's marriage to a papist, idolater, or any unbeliever; do not tempt God by exposing them to a yoke with the unfaithful.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: they must beware that they do not tempt God, and venture their children to walke in that way which so many haue fallen in.

items.text: Permit your child to marry if they are disposed to marriage and lack the gift of continence; do not forbid marriage altogether.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: God commaundeth them to permit and suffer euery one to marrie, that is disposed to marrie.

items.text: If you forbid certain marriages, direct your child to a suitable godly spouse, as Isaac directed Jacob.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: when Isaack forbad his sonne Iacob to marrie any of the daughters of Canaan, he did not restraine him altogether from marriage: and therefore he directed him, where, and with whom he should marrie.

items.text: Exercise your authority over your child under the Lord; deal with them according to God's revealed will, not your own pleasure.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: fathers and mothers must consider, that they haue rule ouer their children vnder the Lord; so that the Lord is aboue them

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.

items.text: Love her sincerely; put up with her weaknesses and do not quickly become bitter or angry, but treat her discreetly and patiently.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: that he vnfainedly loue her, out of which fountaine springeth this dutie, that he must beare with her infirmities

items.text: Protect her; take thought for her safety and well-being.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: to protect her, to haue regard and care ouer her

items.text: Live wisely and discreetly with her; do nothing that rightly offends or provokes her; do not waste the household, return drunk, or speak bitterly.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: he ought in such wisedome, reason and discretion to beare himselfe, that he giue his wife no iust occasion of offence

items.text: Do not deal with her as a servant by doling out money in distrust; let her share the keeping and use of your common property.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: intreate her not as a seruant, by giuing her money as it were in mistrust

items.text: Hold your goods in common; let neither say 'this is mine' but 'this is ours'; share debts as well.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: can neither of them say, this is mine; but this is ours

items.text: Pray together daily for grace to live in peace and love and to help each other toward salvation.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: daily pray to God to giue them grace to liue together in peace and loue, and that each may be an helpe to others saluation

items.text: Enjoy marriage without letting it pull you from God; do not let it make you slack in any duty to God or neighbor, nor let its troubles drive you to break the bond.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: so enioying the commodity and contentation of marriage, that the benefit of their coniunction breed no diuorce betweene God and them

items.text: Do not say of your goods or yourself, 'I will do with my own what I list'; you are not your own but your husband's.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: she may not say, I will do with mine owne what I list: for she her selfe is not her owne, but her husbands

items.text: Do not be a spendthrift or idle; work and steward your means so that your wife and children are not reduced to want.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: who being prodigall, great spenders, or idle and slacke in their businesse, do cause their wiues and children to languish in pouertie

items.text: Do not bruise or break her; she is a weaker vessel, so handle her with gentleness and discretion.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: not to the end that he striuing with so fraile a vessell, should bruise and breake it, but that by gentle and discreet intreating

items.text: Do not break the bond of marriage or live apart; fulfill the duty to live together.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: must not dissolue, or breake the bond of marriage, and their duties to liue together

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Pray earnestly that the natural corruptions you have passed on may be prevented in your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: praying that their naturall corruptions may be preuented in their posterities

items.text: When you see sins in your child, examine your own heart whether they come from you, and repent with prayer.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: enter into thine owne heart, examine thy selfe whether they are not come from thee

items.text: Correct the corrupt nature in your child with the mildest means and least rigor, armed with prayer.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: correct nature in thy childe, which he could not helpe, arming thy selfe with prayer, repenting with Iacob

items.text: Do not teach your children to speak corruptly or act wickedly when they are young, only to beat them for it when they are old.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: teach their children to speake corruptly, and do wickedly whilest they are young

items.text: Do not embolden your little ones to practice iniquity towards others, lest it return upon yourself.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: imbolden their little ones to practise iniquitie towards others

items.text: Give your children no corrupt example at home by carelessness, profaneness, or ungodliness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: beware they giue their children no corrupt example at home, by any carelesnesse, prophanenesse, or vngodlinesse

items.text: Teach your children from a young age; do not leave them untaught until ten or twelve, or they will become headstrong.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: let them go so vntaught, and they will grow so head-strong, that they will sooner be broken then bended

items.text: Use timely discipline: a stripe or two words early will do more good than a hundred stripes later.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: one stripe, or two words, will do more good to a child in time, then an hundred stripes afterward

items.text: After disciplining your child, do not show a merry countenance, lest you undo the good of your correction.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: shewing a merrie countenance after their discipline vsed, then they do good by their chastisement of them whiles they do correct them

items.text: Correct your child with natural affection and Christian compassion, not with brutish unmercifulness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: a Christian kind of compassion in all our censures

items.text: Use mild and affable speech to your children, but without unseemly lenity or foolish behavior.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: we wish it to be voyd of all vnseemely lenitie, and without all shew of foolish, vaine, and vnnecessary behauiour

items.text: Begin discipline and give religion room at home; reform your own household before seeking to reform the church.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: vnlesse they will begin discipline in reforming their houses, & giue religion some roome at home, they shall trauell much and profit little

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Govern your children so that they fear you out of love and reverence, not only from fear of punishment.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: let all parents alwayes labour, that their children may rather feare them for loue and reuerence, then for fearé of punishment

items.text: Set before your children a pattern of godly and honest living, so that they may look into your lives as into a mirror.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: shew themselues vnto their children as a manifest patterne or example

items.text: Maintain natural love and concord among your children; do not allow any spark of hatred to enter their hearts.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: nourishing and maintaining naturall loue and concord amongst the children

items.text: Treat all your children with equality, as nearly as possible, both in daily dealings and in dividing goods.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: are to vse equalitie among their children, so neare as may be, whether in their ordinary vsage, or in the diuision of their goods

items.text: Guard your words and deeds in the house; do not commit any lewd or wicked act, or speak filthy, ribald, or lying words in your children's presence.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: take heede, what they say or do in their houses, and that they do not commit any leude or wicked deed

items.text: Rebuke your servants sharply if they show any lewd or dishonest behavior in the presence of your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Seruants also are to be looked vnto, and sharply rebuked, if they do commit or shew any leud trickes, or vnhonest behauiour in the presence of children

items.text: Keep your children from evil company and dishonest pastimes, lest they hurt their souls.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: parents ought to be circumspect and warie, that their children do not haunt or vse euill companie; nor vse any vnhonest pastime

items.text: Keep your children from lazy idleness, for God has appointed every man to a lawful calling.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: keepe their children from all lazie idlenesse

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Endeavor to get enough knowledge and nurture that you may instruct your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: they must indcuour to get so much nurture and knowledge, as that they may be able to instruct others vnder them

items.text: Do not only provide food and clothing; care also for their spiritual good.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: prophanenesse of many parents, who so they may prouide liuelyhood and necessaries for their children, they care for no more

items.text: Place them only with godly masters and dames who can train them in God's service.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: make choise of such maisters and dames for their children, as are godly and religious, wise hearted, such as are both able and well disposed

items.text: Visit them often, see how they profit, and encourage their governors to be good to them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: they must so often as conueniently they may, repaire vnto them, and see how they profit, and hold them vp by their good counsell

items.text: See that your children learn some occupation or liberal science, to earn an honest living or serve the commonwealth.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Parents must be very carefull that their children may learne some occupation, or profession of life

items.text: Teach them good manners: fair speech, modesty, salutations, gratitude, and confession of offenses.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: First, parents must teach their children to vse faire speech

items.text: Do not treat your servant as a brute beast; give him godly nurture and instruction.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: All these sin and trespasse against the will and word of God, because they are contrary to good nurture and godly instruction

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Teach them good manners and civil behavior: rise before betters, uncover the head, make obeisance, be courteous to equals, gentle to inferiors, and kind to all.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: parents must teach their children good manners, and ciuill behauiour, to rise vp to their betters, to vncouer the head, to make obeysance, to be curteous towards their equals

items.text: Admonish them to let elders and betters speak first, keep silence while they are in place until spoken to, answer in few words directly, and not interrupt or trouble others speaking.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: to giue their elders and betters leaue to speake before them... keepe silence while their betters are in place, vntill they be spoken vnto

items.text: Teach them to frame their gestures to a reverent and dutiful behavior towards others: meet those coming, rise before elders, stand while betters sit, bend the knee, give chief place, and uncover the head.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: parents ought to teach their children how to frame their gestures to a reuerent and dutifull behauiour towards others

items.text: Rise up before the hoary head and honor the person of the old man.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Thou shalt rise vp before the hoar-head, and honour the person of the old man

items.text: Give elders and betters the first opportunity to speak; keep silence while they are in place until spoken to, and answer in few words.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: giue their elders and betters leaue to speake before them

items.text: Stand while betters are sitting, give them the chief place, and uncover your head as a courtesy.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: stand while their betters are sitting in place... giue the chiefe place to their betters... vncouer their head

items.text: Be courteous toward those of the same age or station.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: be curteous towards their equals

items.text: Be gentle and lovely toward those younger or lower in station.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: be gentle and louely to their inferiours

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.

items.text: Do not give any liking or speech of marriage without the consent of your parents or those set over you by them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: they should not so much as giue any liking, much lesse speech of marriage, without the consent of parents, or of those which are set ouer them by their parents

items.text: Let your parents bestow you in marriage, and do not marry without their consent and direction.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: they should not marrie without the consent and direction of their parents, but that they be at their bestowing

items.text: Honor your father and mother, as the fifth commandment commands, and expect blessing or curse accordingly.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: children are commaunded to honour their fathers and mothers, with a blessing promised to those which performe the same

items.text: Do not make a vow that binds you without your parents' consent, for they have authority over your vows.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: parents haue authoritie ouer the vowes of their children

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Since the fewer children you have, the more diligently bring each one up; do not let an hour's fond indulgence leave them to wantonness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: so much more diligently to bring vp their children, by how much they are fewer

items.text: Do not let a cruel love keep them from discipline; that over-indulgence gives them over to all naughtiness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: this is cruell loue, so to loue their children, that they should be (as it were) giuen ouer of their mothers vnto all naughtinesse

items.text: Spend willingly on their instruction in virtue and godliness; do not grudge the cost as if it were wasted on them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: be much more carefull that an horse be well framed to vauting & leaping, then that their child be well instructed to vertue.

items.text: Exercise their minds in godliness as you would till a field; an uncultivated wit brings forth weeds of wantonness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: if he shall leaue the wits of his children vnlooked vnto; and vnexercised, he shall be sure to reape most abundant fruite of wantonnesse and vngraciousnesse.

items.text: Correct your affections toward your children: grieve over their ignorance, impiety, and sins, not only their natural defects or offenses against you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: let parents therefore learne to correct their affections to their children, and be grieued for ignorance, impietie, and sinnes

items.text: Sanctify the marriage bed with prayer against your corruptions and for a holy seed; do not beget children as brute beasts without the fear of God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: when they make no conscience to sanctifie the marriage bed with prayer

items.text: Offer the fruit of the womb to the Lord by good and virtuous bringing up, that your child by carnal generation may become God's child by spiritual regeneration.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: to offer it to the Lord, that their child by carnall generation, may be the child of God by spirituall regeneration.

items.text: Seek your children from God by prayer, as the godly did of old; ask for a holy seed.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: noble and notable men commended vnto vs for rare examples of vertue and godlinesse, were children asked and obtained of God by prayer.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Instruct and bring up your children, even from the cradle, in the fear and nurture of the Lord.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: do instruct and bring vp their children (euen frō the cradle) in the feare & nurture of the Lord

items.text: Bring them up in shamefastness, hatred of vice, and love of all virtue.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: bring them vp in shame fastnesse, hatred of vice, and loue of all vertue

items.text: Be unto your children examples of all godliness and virtue.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: they be vnto their children examples of all godlinesse and vertue

items.text: Keep them from idleness, and bring them up either in learning or in some good art or occupation, that they may get their living with honesty and truth.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
