items.quote: keep them from idlenesse, the mother of all mischiefes, and bring them vp either in learning, or in some good art or occupation, whereby they may get their liuing with honestie and truth

items.text: Present your child to baptism with all convenient speed, and there give the name to your child.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: the fathers dutie, with all conuenient speed to present the child to baptisme, and there to giue the name vnto his child

items.text: Give your children such names as are named and commended in the holy Scriptures, that hearing those names they may be excited to follow virtue.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: would give them such names as are named and commended unto us in the holy Scriptures, to the end that they may be excited to follow virtue

items.text: Call upon God's help by earnest prayer, that he would preserve your children from the snares, subtleties, and temptations of Satan.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: oftentimes call vpon Gods helpe by earnest prayer, that he in mercy would vouthsafe to preserue them from the manifold snares; subtilties, and temptations of Sathan

items.text: Owe to their body nourishment, bringing up, apparel, and sometimes correction, to keep them in awe.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: Vnto the body they owe nourishment, bringing vp, apparell, and sometimes correction, that they may keepe children in awe

items.text: Catechise and instruct them in the doctrine of godliness, that they may keep a good conscience before God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: Vnto the soule they owe catechising, instruction, and doctrine: and that of two sorts; namely, of godlinesse, and of ciuilitie. By the one, they shall keepe a good conscience before God

items.text: Instruct them in civility, that they may obtain a good report among men.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: by the other, they shall obtaine a good report among men

items.text: Do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in instruction and information of the Lord.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children.
items.quote: Ye fathers prouoke not your children to wrath, but bring them vp in instruction, and information of the Lord

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.

items.text: Honor your father and your mother, that you may live long in the land the Lord your God gives you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: the Lord addeth this promise, That thy dayes may be long in the land which the Lord thy God giueth thee

items.text: Be a glory to your father and not a shame to him.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: what a shame it is to be a shame vnto your fathers, to whom ye ought to be a glory

items.text: Be a joy to your mother and not a grief to her.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: ye may be a glory to your fathers, and a ioy to your mothers

items.text: Live so as to wipe away your father's tears and stay your mother's sorrow.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: wipe away the teares of griefe from your fathers eyes, and stay the mournfull and sorrowfull spirits of your tender mothers

items.text: Do not blame your parents for your own sin; you are without excuse.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: hope to shelter their sinnes vnder their parents defaults, are plainly left without excuse

items.text: By honoring and pleasing your parents, seek to be blessed in their prayers; fear their curse.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: by honouring and pleasing them, seeke to be blessed in their prayers

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Love your children, for you are bound by the law of nature to love those you have begotten and borne.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Parents are bound by the law of nature to loue their children: for what a crueltie were it, not to loue them that they haue begotten and borne?

items.text: Hide your love from your children, especially those of some discretion, so they do not take boldness to do as they list.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: wisedome requireth, that they some what dissemble and hide their loue... lest they should take boldnesse thereupon, to do what they list.

items.text: Use the rod of correction on your children; do not spare it, or you hate your son and share in his death.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: He which spareth the rod, hateth his sonne.

items.text: Do not smile, laugh, kiss, or commend your children when they do evil; sharply reprove them and show your displeasure.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: neuer smile or laugh at any words or deeds of their children, done lewdly, vnhonestly, naughtily, wantonly, or shamefully, not to kisse and commend them for so doing.

items.text: Kiss and make much of your children when they do anything that is a sign of goodness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: let them kisse and make much of them, whensoeuer they shall see or heare them do any thing that is a signe of goodnesse.

items.text: Do not set your child in the place of God or love them more than God, lest God take them away.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: to set their child, or any thing else in the roome of God, and so loue the same aboue him which gaue it

items.text: Bring them up well and virtuously from their tender age, and instruct them in virtue from infancy; this is the best inheritance.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: there can none more precious and better heritage be left vnto children, then if they be well and vertuously brought vp from their tender age

items.text: Do not allure your children to evil by your lewd example, nor neglect to instruct them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: by their leud example allure to naughtinesse, or neglect due instruction

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Instruct and correct them in the fear of God, using doctrine and discipline at home and joining your help with magistrate and minister to keep them from corruption.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: fathers of families vse not doctrine and discipline in their houses, and ioyne their helping hands to Magistrates and Ministers

items.text: Endeavor to bring them into the covenant and make them children of God by grace.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Bring thy children within the compasse of the couenant, indeuour to make thy sonne the sonne of God, and thy daughter by nature, the daughter of God by grace

items.text: Teach them the judgments of the Lord.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: teach them with Abraham the iudgements of the Lord

items.text: Pray for them that they may live in the light of the Lord.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: pray for them with Abraham, that they may liue in the light of the Lord

items.text: Offer them to God as a holy sacrifice, dedicating them to his service.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: be readie to offer them with Abraham, that they may be an holy sacrifice vnto the Lord

items.text: Use every good and godly means to bring them up well, so that you may see them as children of God and heirs of the covenant.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: we exhort parents to the ordinary meanes to bring vp their children, so as they may see them the children of God, as heires of the couenant

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Provide for their bodily needs: feed them, clothe them, and nourish them with necessary sustenance.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: It is not enough to seed them, to cloath them, and to nourish their bodies with necessary sustenance.

items.text: Do not seek to provide for them by oppressing the poor, wronging the widow and fatherless, or breaking God's commandments.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: they oppresse the poore and needie, and do wrong to the widdow and the fatherlesse

items.text: Instruct them in the grounds of Christian religion, teach them the fear of God and his will, and catechize them in youth.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Catechise a child in his youth, and he will remember it when he is old.

items.text: Lead them in a virtuous life, and rebuke and chastise them for ill doing.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: to leade their life vettuously, and to rebuke them, and chastise them for ill doing

items.text: Labor diligently to have all vices and abuses, especially irreverence and neglect of public worship, corrected in your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: they must labour with all diligence, that they may be redressed and amended in their children and seruants

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.

items.text: Reverence your parents with humility, modest shamefacedness, and awe, standing in fear of them and seeking to please rather than offend them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: children carry towards their parents, a certaine honest and modest shamefastnesse, ioyned with a bashfull awfulnesse, and standing in feare of them

items.text: Obey your parents willingly, without murmuring or grudging; submit to their direction and rule, doing all lawful commands and refraining from what they forbid.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: willingly, without murmuring or grudging they be willing to be ordered, directed, guided, and ruled by their parents

items.text: Be thankful to your parents for all benefits received; remain ever mindful of their kindness, and never offer them any discourtesy or occasion of unkindness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: alwayes mindfull of benefits receiued, and therefore carryeth continually a vigilant and watchfull eye towards the partie by whom it hath bene pleasured, that no discourtesie in any case be offered

items.text: Do not marry without your parents' consent, for that breaks reverence, obedience, and thankfulness toward them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: they bestow themselues in marriage without the consent of their parents, there they do fault

items.text: If your father has chosen a spouse for you who is not wicked, deformed, or of a contrary religion, submit to his choice.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: their fathers hauing prouided for them such as are not of a wicked life, nor deformed, nor euill-fauoured, nor of a contrary religion, they should submit themselues vnto their choyce

items.text: If you cannot yet accept your father's choice, pray earnestly that God would direct your parents in a godly choice and subdue your own reluctance to submit.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: desire him to direct their parents in a godly and fit choyce, but also to subdue in them this corrupt affection

items.text: Provide for your parents in their old age; feed and care for them as they cared for you, and make some recompense for their pains.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: to prouide meate, and feed their dams, when through age they grow so old that they are not able to helpe themselues

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Parents towards their children.

items.text: Provide for your children's needs in this life, offering counsel and advice.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: to giue their children that which may helpe them in this life, to counsell

items.text: Provide fit and religious marriages for your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: to prouide them fit and religious marriages

items.text: Do not forbid marriage solely because the chosen partner is not wealthy, if that partner is honest, religious, and godly.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: although they be not so rich and wealthie as they would wish them to match with, yet they ought not to hinder... their children to marrie, onely for want of goods and substance

items.text: Ensure your children marry at an age of understanding, and advise them to choose according to their condition.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: Parents ought to be carefull, that their children do marrie in such an age wherein they should vnderstand whom they choose... and that they do not seeke to match themselues in marriage aboue their degree

items.text: Do not force or compel your children into marriage against their will, nor sell them for gain.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: parents to sell their children for gaine... and to marrie them when they list, and to whom they list, without the good liking of their children

items.text: Ensure mutual affection (knitting of hearts) before agreeing to a marriage.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: there must and ought to be a knitting of hearts before striking of hands

items.text: Choose suitable husbands for your daughters and wives for your sons.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: they should be carefull in time, to make meete choise of husbands for their daughters, and fit wiues for their sonnes

items.text: Govern mildly and gently; do not turn fatherly rule into tyranny, especially in marriage choices.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: let them abstaine from all rigour and roughnesse, and beware that they turne not their fatherly iurisdiction and gouernment, into a tyrannicall sowrenesse and waywardnesse

items.text: Win your children's hearts by love, not by slavish terror; aim for reverent obedience.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: must carrie such an euen and vpright hand... that they may by loue seeke to winne the hearts... not to keepe them vnder a seruile or slauish awe

items.text: Do not arrange marriages from greed or self-interest; do not force a match your child cannot accept.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: they be free from all sinister and corrupt affection, and that for luker and couetousnesse they seeke not to thrust such matches vpon their children, as they cannot brooke nor like well of

items.text: Begin the marriage arrangement with prayer, seeking God's guidance and obedience to his word.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: but that they begin it with prayer: that in the whole action they may in such sort be directed, that they do nothing against the word of God

items.text: Be examples of godliness and virtue; avoid doing or saying evil or offensive things before your children.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: to be themselues examples of all godlinesse and vertuousneste to their children. So that they must remember, that they themselues do not say, or do any thing that is euill, or offensiue, in the presence of their children

items.text: Prevent fights and injuries among your children; sharply reprimand swearing, cursing, lying, bawdy talk, or unchristian songs.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Parents towards their children
items.quote: They must be circumspect that their children do not fight, and iniurie one another; and if they sweare, curse, lye, or speake any bawdie or ribaldous words, or sing any... vnchristian songs, then to reprooue them sharply for it

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.

items.text: Labor to banish sin and corrupt religion out of your dwellings, and be a lantern of godly life, that your servants may direct their lives after your good example.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: labour to banish sinne and corrupt religion out of their dwellings, and to be a lanterne of godly life

items.text: Behave yourself with your servants: be not too familiar with them, but admonish them often; yet do not discourage them from well-doing, and be not too severe or too partial; moderate all by discretion.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: not too familiar with them, which many times breedeth contempt, but he is to admonish them often, and yet he must not discourage them

items.text: Esteem and account well of your servants, and use your authority over them mildly and Christianly, being as a father unto them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: all maisters are in conscience bound to esteeme and account well of their seruants, and to vse their authoritie that they haue ouer them, mildly and Christianly

items.text: So dispose and order your affairs that you absent yourself from home as little as may be, for all things are well and fitly done when the master is present.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: a maister of a family should so dispose and order his affaires and businesse, that he depart and absent himselfe from home as little as may be

items.text: Live in such sort that you be not noted either a miser for your keeping, or prodigal for your spending.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: they ought to liue in such sort, that they be not noted either misers for their keeping, or prodigall for their spending

items.text: Use the riches God has given you well, both to your own comfort and the good of your neighbor; be not a covetous niggard.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: he hath not the grace to vse his riches well, either to his owne comfort, or the good of his neighbour

items.text: When you hire servants, be as careful and inquisitive of their honesty, godly conversation, and knowledge of God's religion, as of their skill in their art.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: when they go about to hire any seruants, would be no lesse carefull and inquisitiue of their honestie, godly conuersation, and how they haue profited in the knowledge of God his religion

items.text: Have care over the bodies of your servants.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: As house-holders ought to haue care ouer the bodies of their seruants

items.text: Have much more care over their souls; kindle them in zeal of God, longing to teach and utter knowledge as a nurse to empty her breasts.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: so much more ouer their soules... kindle them in zeale of God, longing to teach and vtter knowledge, as a nurse to empty her breasts

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.

items.text: Love your father and mother with all your heart.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: they loue them with all their hearts

items.text: Fear and dread them as those who stand in God's place toward you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: they feare and dread them

items.text: Cheerfully carry out all their commands, will, and lawful desires.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: they cheerfully do their commandements, will, and pleasure

items.text: Seek their honor, reputation, profit, and advancement in all lawful things.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: they seeke their worship, credite, profit, and preferment in all things lawfull

items.text: If need require, give your lives for them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: if need require, that they giue their liues for them

items.text: Remember that you are your parents' possession and owe them your very self and all you are able to do.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: they are their parents goods and possessions; and that they owe to them, euen their owne selues, and all that they are able to do

items.text: Continue in childlike affection and love even when they treat you harshly, bearing their reproofs patiently.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: still continue and declare their child-like affection and loue

items.text: Testify your inward reverence by outward signs: rise to meet them, bow before them, and seat them in the place of honor.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: arole from his seate, came to meete her, bowed before her, and seated her vpon his right hand

items.text: Do not despise your parents or withhold the name of father and mother, even if they are of meaner estate than you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: many children when they come to honor or wealth, do so despise their parents, if they be of meaner calling then themselues, that hardly they will acknowledge, or call them father

items.text: Defend your parents' honor against false opinions and slanders, and do not allow others to hold them in contempt.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: we should so esteeme of them, as that neither we our selues should despise them, nor suffer others-to haue them in contempt

items.text: Do not expose your parents' shame or lay them open to the scorn of others.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: lay them open to the scorne of others

items.text: Give them necessary assistance and hospitality in their need.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.
items.quote: entertainment, and necessarie assistance that children owe to their parents

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The dutie of Children towards their Parents. · The summe and effect of all which, is as followeth.

items.text: Reverence, love, and always have a care for them as sent by God.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: reuerently esteeme of them... reuerence, loue, and alwayes haue a care of them: if for nothing else, yet for the Lords sake

items.text: Aid them in old age and need, and give all you have for their good.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: aide them in their old age and vnweildy crookednesse... do wholly bestow themselues, and all that they haue to do them good withall

items.text: Do not answer roughly, smite, curse, or speak evil of them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: ought not to giue them a rough or stubburne answer... neither to smite, or curse, or speake euill of their father and mother

items.text: When they are justly angry, submit to them or you cannot regain God's favor.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: when their parents are iustly angrie with them... vntill they haue submitted themselues to their father and mother

items.text: Do to them as you would have your own children do to you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: so to do and behaue themselues to their parents... as they would haue their children... do, and behaue themselues to them

items.text: Be governed by them, follow their good example, and diligently discharge your duty.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: follow the good examples of their fathers and mothers, and to suffer themselues to be gouerned by them... bestow all paine and diligence to discharge their dutie towards them

items.text: Do not live as you please while they have rule over you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: they are not at their owne libertie, to do as they list, so long as they haue a father and mother to rule them

items.text: Love and help one another; do not fall out.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: they must not fall out among themselues, but naturally loue and helpe one another

items.text: For life, love them; for maintenance, obey them; for instruction, revere them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The dutie of Children towards their Parents
items.quote: for life, they owe loue: for maintenance, they owe obedience: for instruction, they owe reuerence

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.

items.text: Instruct and catechize your servants in the grounds and principles of Christian religion.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: a maister in his familie hath all the offices of Christ; for he must rule, and teach, and pray

items.text: Correct your servants with such reproofs and corrections that you do not provoke them to wrath but win them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: vse such reproofes, and such corrections, that you do not prouoke them, but moue them; that you do not exasperate them, but win them

items.text: In their sickness, lodge them apart, cherish and nourish them with more choice and dainty meat, and visit them.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: the sicke are to be seuerally lodged from the whole, and to be cherished and nourished with more choise and daintie meate

items.text: Do not make yourself too familiar with your servants, but behave modestly and wisely so that they may fear, reverence, and stand in awe of you as the mistress and mother of the house.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: the mistrisse or dame, do not make her selfe too familiar with her seruants

items.text: Correct your men-servants yourself; do not leave it to your wife, for a man scorns to be beaten by a woman.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: the master should correct the men, and the mistris her maides

items.text: Correct your maid-servants yourself; do not leave it to your husband, for a maid's nature is corrupted with the stripes of a man.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: the master should correct the men, and the mistris her maides

items.text: Before your death, set order for your household and exhort and pray for religion, uprightness, peace and order after you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: setting order for all things at their death, with especiall exhortations and prayers for religion, for vprightnesse in their callings, for peace and order after them

items.text: Receive no servant into your house but one you can govern; if a wicked one has crept in, put him out.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.
items.quote: maisters should receiue none into their houses, but whom they can gouerne as Ioshua did: and if any such haue crept into their doores, they must put him forth againe

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters.

items.text: Obey and perform their labors cheerfully and willingly, with fear and trembling, as unto Christ, even in their absence.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: do frō their hearts, cheerefully, and willingly, performe the labours and workes that their maisters... shall command them... reuerently, and faithfully to obey... with feare and trembling, in singlenesse of heart, as vnto Christ... as well in the absence... as in presence.

items.text: Be faithful in what is committed to him, keeping his goods so carefully that he can find any necessary even in the dark.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: they be faithfull in things committed to them... that so they may keepe their goods... whatsoeuer goods... they shall haue charge of... they carefully see such things so well and orderly placed... they can presently fetch the same.

items.text: Do not corrupt the wife, children, or fellow servants by evil counsel or lewd behavior.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: they be carefull to obserue vprightnesse of manners, that the wife, sonnes and daughters, or other fellow seruants, be not corrupted by their bad counsels, or lewd behauiour.

items.text: Love them and be affected toward them as a dutiful child is to his father.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: to loue them, and to be affectioned towards them, as a dutifull child is to his [father].

items.text: Be reverent and lowly in words and gestures; bear with their angry words and do not answer back spitefully.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: be reuerent and lowly to them in their words and gestures, to suffer and forbeare them... forbeare... their angrie... words, and in no wise answer againe spitefully.

items.text: Be faithful in deeds and promises, and do not be overly bold to dally with his wife, daughters, or maidens.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: be faithfull and trustie to them and theirs: in deedes and promises... not ouer boldly to dallie with their maisters wife, daughters, or maidens.

items.text: Endeavor to the uttermost to procure their honesty, credit, and profit, even when absent.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: carefully endeuour to do and procure... that which may be to their maisters... honestie, credit and profit, and that as well when they are absent and out of sight.

items.text: If you have displeased them, reconcile and ask forgiveness at once; do not run away.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: if they do [anger], they ought incontinent... to reconcile themselues... and to aske them forgiuenesse... nor... run away.

items.text: Obey only so far as Christian religion allows; refuse dishonest, unlawful, wicked, or ungodly commands.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: so farre as Christian religion suffereth... if their maisters shall command them to do any thing that is vnhonest, vnlawful, wicked... they must in no wise obey it.

items.text: For maid-servants: be careful, faithful, patient, neat, and pleasing; honest in word, deed, and attire; diligent in household skills, chiefly holding your peace.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: The conditions of a good maid-seruant, are, that she be carefull, faithfull, patient, neat, and pleasing... honest in her word, deed, and attire: diligent in an houshold... but chiefly in holding her peace.

items.text: Help one another when one is overburdened, as one part of the body eases another.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: one therefore should helpe another, as we see by vse in our owne bodies, when one leg is weary, we can rest it on the other.

items.text: Command the negligent, loitering servant to help the weary and overcharged one.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, The Seruants dutie towards their Maisters
items.quote: then should the maister himselfe command the negligent and loytering seruant, to helpe and ease the weary, and him that is well imployed and ouer-charged.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.

items.text: Love your wife steadfastly, not variably, and let the marriage union continue no matter what befalls either of you.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: this loue must be stedfast, not variable; and that the vnion of marriage continue notwithstanding, whatsoeuer befall either the husband or the wife.

items.text: Do not ground your love on beauty, riches, or other transient things, but think on the marriage union so that you may enjoy, nourish, and continue that love.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: must euery man thinke vpon this vnion in marriage, that he may enioy, nourish, & continue the loue that there of proceedeth

items.text: Support your wife, be gentle and friendly to her, and forgive her even as God has forgiven you through Christ.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: To be gentle one to another, friendly, and each to forgiue other, euen as God hath forgiuen vs through Christ.

items.text: Do not complain of your wife's defects or infirmities, but bear with them, for such defaults must not break the love that comes from the marriage union.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: neither the head of the body, albeit it be crooked or mishapen. Such defaults do neuer breake vnion and loue betweene the head and the body.

items.text: When your wife speaks sharply or chides without cause, be as if deaf and dumb; do not answer back, but put up with her words.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: the husband put vp many shrewde speeches of his wife, as if he heard them not.

items.text: Leave your father and mother and cleave to your wife, for the marriage union is greater than the bond between child and parent.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: For this cause shall a man leaue his father and mother, and cleaue to his wife.

items.text: Share your secret counsels and affairs with your wife, and seek to please her more than your parents.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: The husband and the wife haue their secret counsels and communication of matters concerning their profit and commodity... the husband more desirous to please his wife, then their Parents.

items.text: Remember that you have married a daughter of Adam with all her infirmities, and resolve to bear what cannot be soon amended.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, 1. The dutie of the Husband towards his Wife.
items.quote: Let the husband think, that he hath married a daughter of Adam, and all her infirmities.

work: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government
heading: What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants.

items.text: Keep them from idleness.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: refraine and keepe their seruants from idlenesse.

items.text: Instruct them by diligent teaching and good example in honesty, good manners, and all virtue.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: by diligent instruction and good example, they bring vp their seruants and housholds, in honestie and comely manners, and in all vertue.

items.text: Teach them the knowledge of their trade thoroughly and honestly, without guile, fraud, delay, or concealing.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: instruct their apprentises and seruants in the knowledge of their occupations and trades, euen as parents would teach their owne children, without all guile, fraud, delaying, or concealing.

items.text: When correction is necessary, give it with discretion, pity, and desire for their amendment, as loving parents.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: giue it them with such discretion, pittie, and desire of their amendment, as louing parents vse to deale with their deare children

items.text: Pay their wages justly and in due time; do not oppress them; and reward their faithful labor bountifully.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: let them bountifully reward the iust and faithfull labour of their seruants, and pay their couenants in a fit and conuenient time

items.text: Provide wholesome meat, drink, and lodging; help, comfort, relieve, and cherish them in sickness and in health.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: prouiding for them wholsome meate, drink, and lodging, and otherwise to helpe them, comfort them, and relieue and cherish them

items.text: Do not overwork them or treat them as beasts; govern them quietly and gently, remembering they are men.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: they may not grieue their seruants with too much labour, but alwayes remember that they are not beasts, but men: so that they ought quietly to gouerne them

items.text: Hear their complaints fairly; do not punish without just cause or with cruel stripes.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: will not heare their seruants speake, but vpon a simple surmise and brain-sicknesse, do euill intreate them by cruell stripes, when in truth there is no iust cause.

items.text: Use mildness and equity toward them; speak to them as brethren and sisters, and deal with them as Christians.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: vse their seruants and apprentises, with mildnesse & equitie... they must speake vnto them as vnto brethren and sisters, & deale with them as with Christians.

items.text: Allow them time to serve God and sanctify the Sabbath; be careful that they live honestly, virtuously, and Christianly.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: make no greater account that their seruants do serue him more carefully then themselues, and sanctifie the Sabbaths.

items.text: Carry the burden of care, travel, and labor for your household.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: the office of a good housholder to carry the burthen of care, trauell, and labour

items.text: Be faithful in ordering his goods and house; see apparel neat; and with your husband give good example, entertain peace, and keep due order.
items.citation: A Godly Forme of Houshold Government, What duties Maisters and Mistresses owe to their seruants
items.quote: the dutie of a wife, to be faithfull in keeping and well ordering of his goods and house... both their duties is, effectually to giue good examples
